asset_name: 「我在场」第一人称历史沉浸结构（瞬间落地-真实性立约-禁入潜入-倒计时撞击-见证崩解）
topic: You're the Worker Who Opened Tutankhamun's Tomb

audience.target_audience: 18-45 悬疑爱好者、美国为主、性别偏男

materials:
一、30秒速览（全部是铁证级事实）
- 图坦卡蒙（Tutankhamun）：古埃及第十八王朝倒数第三位法老，约公元前1332–前1323年在位，约9岁登基，约18–19岁去世。
- 他的陵墓（帝王谷第62号墓，编号KV62）1922年11月4日被英国考古学家霍华德·卡特（Howard Carter）率领、卡那封伯爵（Lord Carnarvon）资助的考古队发现，是迄今唯一基本完好保存至今的古埃及法老陵墓。
- 墓中登记文物5,398件，清理编目耗时约十年（1922–1932）。
- 黄金面具重10.23公斤；最内层人形棺为110.4公斤纯金。
- "法老诅咒"是媒体制造的传说：2002年《英国医学杂志》（BMJ）统计研究证实，进入墓中者的寿命与未进入者无统计学差异。
- 自2025年11月起，5,000余件图坦卡蒙随葬品在新建的大埃及博物馆（Grand Egyptian Museum，吉萨）首次完整集中展出；木乃伊本体仍留在帝王谷原墓中。
二、法老其人：身世与统治
生卒与在位【古代文献+科学研究】
- 生于约公元前1342年，原名图坦卡顿（Tutankhaten，意为"阿顿神的活化身"）；登基后改名图坦卡蒙（"阿蒙神的活化身"），这个改名本身就是一次宗教转向的公开宣告。
- 约公元前1332年登基（当时约9岁），约公元前1323年去世（约18–19岁），在位约9年。
- 父亲：帝王谷第55号墓（KV55）木乃伊，2010年DNA研究认定其为图坦卡蒙生父，通常被认为是"宗教改革法老"阿肯那顿（Akhenaten）【科学研究：2010年《美国医学会杂志》JAMA。注意：KV55墓主是阿肯那顿还是其弟斯门卡拉，学界仍有争议】。
- 母亲：帝王谷第35号墓中编号KV35YL的"年轻女士"木乃伊，DNA证实她是其丈夫的同胞姐妹——图坦卡蒙是父母近亲（兄妹）婚配的产物【科学研究：JAMA 2010】。
- 妻子：安克赫娜蒙（Ankhesenamun），阿肯那顿与娜芙蒂蒂（Nefertiti）之女，即图坦卡蒙的同父异母姐姐。
- 女儿：墓中出土两具流产胎儿木乃伊（编号317a、317b，孕周约24周和36周），DNA证实为图坦卡蒙的亲生女儿【科学研究】。
统治期间做了什么（有碑文为证）【古代文献】
- 推翻父亲的宗教改革：恢复以阿蒙神（Amun）为首的传统多神信仰，废除阿顿一神教；王室随即从阿玛尔纳（Amarna）迁回孟菲斯。
- 《复位碑》（Restoration Stela）：立于卡纳克神庙，碑文自述登基时"神庙倾颓、诸神背弃、军队失利"，他重建庙宇、重立祭司——这是研究其统治最核心的同时代文献。
- 恢复与米坦尼（Mitanni）的外交关系，在努比亚和近东有军事行动（墓葬壁画与器物有相关题材）。
- 实际掌权者被认为是两位重臣：阿伊（Ay，"神之父"头衔）与军队总司令霍伦海布（Horemheb）——两人先后在他死后继位。
- 死后被除名：霍伦海布时期系统性抹除阿玛尔纳时期法老的名字，后世王表（如阿拜多斯王表）中完全没有图坦卡蒙——这是他一度"在历史上查无此人"的直接原因。
死后一桩悬案（赫梯档案）【古代文献，归属存疑】
- 赫梯文献《苏皮路里乌玛功德录》记载：图坦卡蒙死后，埃及一位王后致信赫梯国王苏皮路里乌玛一世，请求派一位王子来联姻并继承埃及王位；赫梯派出的赞南扎王子在赴埃途中被杀，引发两国长期敌对。
- 信中王后被称为"达哈蒙祖"（Dakhamunzu），主流认为即安克赫娜蒙，但也有学者认为是娜芙蒂蒂或梅利塔顿【争议/存疑：写信者身份未最终确认】。
三、这座墓为何能幸存3300年【考古实物+档案记录】
1. 墓很小：图坦卡蒙暴亡时，他自己的王陵尚未开工，只能把一座非王室规格的小墓改建为陵寝——帝王谷中最小的王室墓，反而成了保护色。
2. 古代只被盗过两次，且很快被修复：走廊杂物中有盗墓者遗留物，两道墓门有"打开—重新封泥"的痕迹，证明下葬后不久遭两次盗掘，但被墓地官员及时重新封堵。学界估计约六成珠宝陪葬品已被盗走【学界估计】。
3. 被建筑垃圾深埋：约公元前12世纪，修建拉美西斯六世墓的工人在其正上方搭建工棚、倾倒碎石，入口被彻底覆盖。
4. 名字被抹除：官方王表删去了他，后人连"该找这座墓"都不知道。
四、发现全程：时间线（档案级精度）【档案记录】
- 1907年：卡那封伯爵开始资助埃及发掘，经埃及文物部门推荐，聘请卡特主持。
- 1914年：卡那封取得帝王谷发掘特许权（接替放弃的美国富豪西奥多·戴维斯）。
- 1917年起：卡特开始地毯式排查帝王谷，一战后一无所获；卡那封决定1922年为最后一年。
- 1922年11月4日：工人在拉美西斯六世墓附近的古代工棚遗迹下发现第一级石阶。卡特给英国的卡那封发电报，原文："终于在帝王谷有了重大发现；一座封印完好的宏伟陵墓；已重新掩埋等候您到来；祝贺。"
- 11月23日：卡那封携女儿伊芙琳·赫伯特女士（Lady Evelyn Herbert）抵达卢克索。
- 11月24日：清出全部16级台阶，封门上发现图坦卡蒙王名圈封印——但门上有古代打开并重新封堵的痕迹，众人一度担心又是一座被盗空的墓。
- 1922年11月26日（人类考古史上的名场面）：卡特在第二道封门左上角凿开小洞，伸入蜡烛窥视。卡那封在身后问："你能看见什么吗？"卡特回答："是的，美妙无比的东西。"（Yes, wonderful things.）
  - 卡特后来回忆原文（《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷）："起初我什么也看不见，墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳。渐渐地，眼睛适应了光线，细节从朦胧中浮现——奇异的动物、雕像，还有黄金，到处都是黄金的闪光。"
- 11月26日深夜（当时未公开）：卡特、助手卡伦德、卡那封与伊芙琳女士四人先行入内查看，成为3300多年来第一批进入墓室的现代人【档案记录：依据卡特私人文件，当时对外未承认】。
- 11月29日：在埃及官员与受邀贵宾见证下正式开墓。
- 1923年2月16日：开启核心的墓室（Burial Chamber）。
- 1924年2月：因不满埃及政府监管与文物归属条款，卡特宣布"罢工"封闭陵墓、辞去职务；1925年1月在新协议下复工——按新条款，全部文物归埃及所有，不再按旧例与发掘方分成。
- 1925年10月28日：开启最内层纯金棺盖，见到包裹中的木乃伊与黄金面具。
- 1925年11月11–19日：在相邻的KV15墓走廊改建的临时实验室里，由卡特、解剖学家道格拉斯·德里（Douglas Derry）和萨利赫·贝伊·哈姆迪（Saleh Bey Hamdi）揭开木乃伊裹布。
- 1932年：全部文物清理、编目、保护完毕——前后约十年。
- 1939年3月2日：卡特病逝于伦敦，终年64岁（患癌症）。他生前对诅咒说嗤之以鼻，留下名言："所有神志健全的人都应以蔑视对待这类无稽之谈。"
当时的传播机制（写文案很好用）：卡那封把独家报道权卖给了伦敦《泰晤士报》，全球其他媒体被挡在门外——这既是发掘经费来源，也直接催生了竞争对手报纸编造花边新闻的动机（见第八部分"诅咒"）。
五、墓室结构与5,398件文物清单【考古实物】
墓室结构（KV62）
一条倾斜走廊连接四个墓室：
1. 前厅（Antechamber）：卡特第一眼看到的地方。镀金动物造型灵床、6辆拆解的战车、王座、储物箱；两尊与真人等大的法老守护者木雕像分立墓室封门两侧。
2. 附厅（Annex）：最小最乱的一间（古代盗墓所致），存放约2,000件日常类物品——食物、葡萄酒罐（标注年份与产地）、油膏、游戏棋、工具等。
3. 墓室（Burial Chamber）：唯一有壁画的房间。北壁画继任者阿伊为法老主持"开口仪式"，另有法老拥抱冥神奥西里斯、天空女神努特等场景；西壁画12只狒狒（《杜阿特之书》第一时辰）。墙壁上有至今可见的褐色斑点——科学研究认为是封墓时灰泥与颜料未干、湿气滋生微生物所致，证明下葬极为仓促【科学研究：盖蒂保护研究所分析】。
4. 珍宝室（Treasury）：豺神阿努比斯镀金神龛镇守；四女神贴面守护的卡诺匹克神龛；多艘陪葬模型船；413件"沙布提"俑（供法老在来世驱使的仆役俑）。

六、明星科学案例：来自天外的匕首【科学研究】
- 木乃伊裹布中共发现两把匕首：一把金刃，一把铁刃（位于右腿侧，全长34.2厘米，金柄、水晶圆头、金鞘刻百合与豺首纹）。铁在公元前14世纪的埃及比黄金珍贵——埃及直到约公元前8世纪才掌握冶铁。
- 2016年，意大利米兰理工大学达妮埃拉·科梅利（Daniela Comelli）团队用便携式X射线荧光光谱（XRF）无损检测刀身：成分为铁+10.8%镍+0.58%钴，镍钴比与陨铁特征高度吻合，与11种已知铁陨石成分相似。论文发表于《陨石学与行星科学》（Meteoritics & Planetary Science，DOI: 10.1111/maps.12664）——"陨铁锻造"从百年猜想变为实证。
- 2022年，日本千叶工业大学松井孝文团队二维面扫描发现刀身保留宽约1毫米的富镍条带（魏德曼花纹特征），该结构在超过约950°C的热加工中会消失——说明匕首是低温锻打成形。
- 同一研究还提出：金柄粘合剂为石灰基（古埃及不用，托勒密时代才出现），结合《阿玛尔纳书信》中米坦尼国王图什拉塔（Tushratta）赠予阿蒙霍特普三世的礼物清单，推测匕首可能来自米坦尼王室馈赠【争议/存疑：产地溯源属研究假说，学界未形成共识】。
七、他怎么死的：从"谋杀说"到科学结论
- 1968年：利物浦大学哈里森（R. G. Harrison）团队X光检查，发现颅腔内有一块游离碎骨——"脑后遭重击谋杀说"流行数十年【已过时】。
- 2005年1月：哈瓦斯（Zahi Hawass）主持对木乃伊进行CT扫描（约1,700张切片）：排除头部遭重击（颅底孔洞系入殓师取脑的标准操作，碎骨与外伤无关）；发现左大腿骨下部严重骨折（靠近膝盖，骨折处无愈合迹象，说明死前不久发生）；估算死亡年龄约18–19岁【科学研究】。
- 2010年2月：《美国医学会杂志》（JAMA）发表DNA研究（哈瓦斯领衔，埃、德、意多国团队）：
  - 木乃伊体内检出恶性疟原虫DNA——迄今最古老的疟疾基因证据之一；
  - 左足第二、三跖骨缺血性骨坏死，足部畸形，结合墓中130余根手杖，推断他行走需拄杖；
  - 确认父母为同胞兄妹（近亲婚配被认为是其多种遗传病的原因）；
  - 综合结论：最可能死于严重疟疾叠加腿部骨折感染等并发症，而非谋杀。
- 2014年：英国广播公司（BBC）纪录片据"虚拟尸检"提出"杵状足、龅牙、女性化髋部"等说法——被哈瓦斯等多位专家公开质疑，属电视传播阶段的夸张【争议/存疑】。
- 文案安全口径："科学已排除谋杀；疟疾+腿伤并发症是目前证据最强的结论，但确切死因仍无法百分之百锁定。"
八、"法老诅咒"：起源、传播与科学辟谣（文案的流量担当，但必须按事实讲）
发生了什么【档案记录】
- 1923年4月5日：资助人卡那封伯爵死于开罗，终年56岁。死因明确：面颊被蚊虫叮咬后感染（刮胡子时加重），发展为丹毒、败血症并发肺炎——当时还没有抗生素。
- 媒体随即炒作：小说家玛丽·科雷利（Marie Corelli）公开警告"擅入者将有严重后果"；柯南·道尔（《福尔摩斯》作者）对《纽约时报》表示"可能有恶灵作祟"；随后金融家乔治·杰伊·古尔德（George Jay Gould）参观墓后死于肺炎（1923年5月16日）等事件被不断叠加入"诅咒名单"。
- 流传最广的"墓中刻着'死亡之翼将降临打扰法老安眠者'"——墓中从未发现任何此类铭文，这是媒体虚构【已辟谣】。
- 传说的背景：卡那封把独家报道权卖给《泰晤士报》，被排斥的竞争对手报纸需要"不需要采访权也能写"的故事——诅咒新闻由此规模化生产。
科学辟谣【科学研究】
- 2002年12月《英国医学杂志》（BMJ），澳大利亚莫纳什大学流行病学家马克·尼尔森（Mark Nelson）根据卡特日记核对了当时在埃及的44名西方人，其中25人属"暴露组"（亲临破封、开棺等关键时刻）：
  - 暴露组平均死亡年龄70岁，未暴露组75岁——校正年龄与性别后无统计学差异；
  - 结论原文："暴露于'木乃伊诅咒'与生存期无显著关联，没有证据支持诅咒存在。"
- 亲手破封的第一责任人霍华德·卡特又活了17年，64岁病逝。
- 卡特的冷静操作：进墓前他曾对墓内空气和石棺表面取样送检——结果"完全无菌"。
- 寿命最长的是全程在场的伊芙琳·赫伯特女士，1980年去世，享年78岁。
- 流传故事警示："卡那封的三条腿狗在主人咽气时嚎叫而死""卡特的金丝雀当天被眼镜蛇吞食"等均为无法证实的轶闻，只能当传说讲，不能当事实写。
九、黄金面具受损与修复事件（2014–2016）【档案记录】
- 2014年8月：开罗埃及博物馆工作人员维修面具展柜照明时碰落面具胡须（胡须重逾2公斤）。
- 工作人员未按规程上报修复，擅自用环氧树脂匆忙粘回，导致胡须粘接偏移、胶体残留在面具表面；清理胶痕时又用手术刀等金属工具刮伤了面具。
- 2015年1月：博物馆承认事件，德国修复专家克里斯蒂安·埃克曼（Christian Eckmann）受邀评估——他指出胡须自1922年出土时即与面具分离（1941年才首次粘合），此次修复可逆。
- 2015年10–12月：德埃联合团队清除环氧树脂，改用蜂蜡（古埃及人实际使用的粘合剂）重新粘接；2015年12月16日面具恢复展出。
- 2016年1月：埃及检察机关以"重大过失"将8名涉事人员（含时任馆长与修复部主任）移送纪律法院，面临罚款直至解职。
- 冷知识：面具出土时胡须与本体分离、分开展示约20年——这次事故在某种意义上"还原了它出土时的样子"。
十、"娜芙蒂蒂密室"之争：一个被科学终结的假说（2015–2018）
- 2015年：英国埃及学家尼古拉斯·里夫斯（Nicholas Reeves）分析高清扫描后提出：墓室北墙与西墙壁画后可能藏有通往另一墓室的门——娜芙蒂蒂的陵墓。证据包括墙面痕迹与面具王名圈疑似被改刻等【争议/存疑】。
- 2016年初：日本雷达专家渡边宏胜的扫描报告称"90%以上存在密室"，时任文物部长背书，轰动全球；但原始数据从未公开。
- 2016年：美国《国家地理》团队第二次雷达扫描未能复现任何密室迹象。
- 2018年2–5月：意大利都灵理工大学弗朗切斯科·波尔切利（Francesco Porcelli）团队进行迄今最严密的第三次探地雷达扫描（垂直+水平双向、双极化高密度采样）。2018年5月6日在第四届国际图坦卡蒙大会上公布结论："以非常高的置信度判定，墓室墙壁后不存在密室或走廊。"埃及文物部宣布此案终结。
- 文案口径：这是"假说—验证—证伪"的完整科学案例，值得讲，但结论必须写"不存在"。
十一、百年展览史与今天：文物都在哪里【档案记录】
- 1972年："图坦卡蒙珍宝展"登陆大英博物馆，伊丽莎白二世女王揭幕，50件文物（含黄金面具），160万人次观展，创下该馆历史纪录；全部60万英镑收益捐赠联合国教科文组织用于菲莱神庙保护。
- 1976–1979年：美国巡展53件文物，七城共超800万人次，开创了"超级大展"（blockbuster）模式。
- 2019–2021年："图坦卡蒙：黄金法老的珍宝"全球告别巡展（150件，其中60件首次出国；巴黎站143万人次创法国纪录）——此后图坦卡蒙文物永久不再离开埃及。
- 2025年11月1日：历时20年建设、耗资约11亿美元的大埃及博物馆（GEM，吉萨金字塔旁）正式开馆，为全球最大单一文明博物馆（馆藏超10万件）；5,000余件图坦卡蒙随葬品首次完整集中展出，黄金面具已移至该馆。
- 木乃伊不在博物馆：1926年10月23日遗体被送回墓中石棺；2005年1月为CT扫描短暂出墓；2007年11月4日（发现85周年）起安放于KV62墓内恒温恒湿玻璃柜中对公众展出；2025年埃及官方确认木乃伊将永久留在帝王谷原墓。
- 帝王谷（含KV62）1979年随"底比斯古城及其墓地"列入世界遗产名录。2014年帝王谷内开放了一座1:1高清复制墓（西班牙Factum Arte制作）供游客替代参观。参观KV62需单独购票。
十二、常见讹传与措辞红线（防踩坑）
可以直接说的（铁证）：
- "1922年11月4日发现、26日'美妙无比的东西'"——卡特电报与著作原文
- "5,398件文物、十年清理"——卡特编目记录
- "黄金面具10.23公斤、最内层金棺110.4公斤纯金"——实测数据
- "匕首是陨铁打造"——2016年同行评审研究
- "墓在古代被盗过两次、约六成珠宝丢失"（后半句加"据学界估计"）
- "父母为同胞兄妹、体内检出疟原虫"——2010年JAMA研究
- "'法老诅咒'无统计学依据"——2002年BMJ研究
必须加限定词的：
- 死因 → "科学排除谋杀；疟疾与腿伤并发症是证据最强的结论，但无法百分之百锁定"
- KV55父亲身份 → "DNA确认为生父，通常认为是阿肯那顿（学界仍有斯门卡拉说）"
- "达哈蒙祖"信件 → "主流认为写信者是安克赫娜蒙，但未最终确认"
- 匕首米坦尼来源 → "研究假说"
- 壁画褐斑成因 → "科学研究主流观点"
绝不能说的：
- "墓中刻有诅咒铭文"（不存在，系媒体虚构）
- "卡那封及发掘者接连暴毙、诅咒应验"（统计研究已否定；卡特本人又活了17年）
- "图坦卡蒙被谋杀"（2005年CT已排除头部重击说）
- "面具毁于2014年事故"（已修复，2015年底恢复展出；且胡须出土时本来就是分离的）
- "娜芙蒂蒂密室已被发现"（2018年雷达已证伪）
- "宝物至今散落欧美"（恰恰相反：全部文物归埃及，现集中在大埃及博物馆）

facts.content: 1922年11月4日，帝王谷（Valley of the Kings），拉美西斯六世墓附近，当地工人在古代工棚遗迹下发现第一级石阶
facts.source: 霍华德·卡特著作《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷；卡特1922年11月6日致卡那封电报

facts.content: 卡特自1917年开始地毯式排查帝王谷，一战后连续数年一无所获；卡那封伯爵决定1922年为最后一年资助
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 卡特给英国卡那封发电报原文：'终于在帝王谷有了重大发现；一座封印完好的宏伟陵墓；已重新掩埋等候您到来；祝贺。'
facts.source: 卡特1922年11月6日电报，参考资料引用

facts.content: 1922年11月26日，卡特在第二道封门左上角凿开小洞，伸入蜡烛窥视。卡那封问：'你能看见什么吗？'卡特回答：'是的，美妙无比的东西。'（Yes, wonderful things.）
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷回忆原文

facts.content: 卡特回忆：'起初我什么也看不见，墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳。渐渐地，眼睛适应了光线，细节从朦胧中浮现——奇异的动物、雕像，还有黄金，到处都是黄金的闪光。'
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷

facts.content: 1922年11月26日深夜（当时未公开），卡特、助手卡伦德、卡那封与伊芙琳女士四人先行入内查看，成为3300多年来第一批进入墓室的现代人
facts.source: 参考资料：依据卡特私人文件，当时对外未承认

facts.content: 1922年11月29日在埃及官员与受邀贵宾见证下正式开墓
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 墓中登记文物5,398件，清理编目耗时约十年（1922-1932）
facts.source: 卡特编目记录，参考资料引用

facts.content: 黄金面具重10.23公斤纯金
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录（藏品号JE 60672）

facts.content: 最内层人形棺为110.4公斤纯金
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 1922年11月23日卡那封抵达后，清出全部16级台阶，封门上发现图坦卡蒙王名圈封印
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 封门上有古代打开并重新封堵的痕迹，证明下葬后不久遭两次盗掘，但被墓地官员及时重新封堵。学界估计约六成珠宝陪葬品已被盗走
facts.source: 参考资料考古记录与学界估计

facts.content: 约公元前12世纪，修建拉美西斯六世墓的工人在其正上方搭建工棚、倾倒碎石，入口被彻底覆盖
facts.source: 参考资料考古记录

facts.content: 前厅（卡特第一眼看到的房间）：镀金动物造型灵床、6辆拆解的战车、礼仪王座、储物箱；两尊与真人等大的法老守护者木雕像分立墓室封门两侧
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单

facts.content: 礼仪王座：木胎包金嵌银与彩陶；靠背为阿玛尔纳风格名画：王后安克赫娜蒙在太阳光芒下为法老涂抹香油。卡特称其为'迄今埃及出土最美之物'
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单，卡特评价

facts.content: 墓室是唯一有壁画的房间。北壁画继任者阿伊为法老主持'开口仪式'；西壁画12只狒狒（《杜阿特之书》第一时辰）。墙壁上有至今可见的褐色斑点——科学研究认为是封墓时灰泥与颜料未干、湿气滋生微生物所致，证明下葬极为仓促
facts.source: 参考资料与盖蒂保护研究所分析

facts.content: 卡特自1917年起在帝王谷地毯式排查，至1922年发现，坚持约5-6年
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 卡那封携女儿伊芙琳·赫伯特女士（Lady Evelyn Herbert）于1922年11月23日抵达卢克索，她是破封时在场的四人之一
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 木乃伊裹布中发现铁刃匕首（位于右腿侧，全长34.2厘米，金柄、水晶圆头）。2016年意大利团队用XRF检测：成分为铁+10.8%镍+0.58%钴，与陨铁特征高度吻合。铁在公元前14世纪的埃及比黄金珍贵
facts.source: 2016年《陨星学与行星科学》（Meteoritics & Planetary Science，DOI: 10.1111/maps.12664）

facts.content: 图坦卡蒙约公元前1332年登基（当时约9岁），约公元前1323年去世（约18-19岁），在位约9年
facts.source: 参考资料古代文献+科学研究综合

facts.content: 从图坦卡蒙下葬（约公元前1323年）到1922年开启，墓封存约3245年

facts.content: 四层镀金木神龛层层套在石棺之外，最外层大到几乎填满墓室
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单

facts.content: 1924年2月卡特因不满埃及政府监管宣布'罢工'辞职；1925年1月在新协议下复工（全部文物归埃及，不再分成）。1932年清理完毕。1939年3月2日卡特病逝于伦敦，终年64岁
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.slot: 卡那封之死与诅咒辟谣
facts.content: 1923年4月5日卡那封伯爵死于开罗（面颊蚊虫叮咬感染发展为败血症），终年56岁。2002年《英国医学杂志》研究：对比44名西方人，25人'暴露组'平均死亡年龄70岁，未暴露组75岁，校正后无统计学差异。卡特本人又活了17年至64岁
facts.source: 2002年12月《英国医学杂志》（BMJ），澳大利亚莫纳什大学马克·尼尔森研究

facts.content: 1920年代帝王谷考古营地条件：沙漠高温、无现代设施、需从尼罗河运水、帐篷营地、煤油灯照明
facts.source: 参考资料背景与卡特日记记载

facts.content: 当地埃及工人是1922年11月4日发现第一级石阶的直接发现者；发掘团队雇佣大量当地劳工进行挖掘与搬运
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 1922年11月4日发现台阶后，卡特立即发电报并重新掩埋现场，等待卡那封从英国赶来，等待时间约19天（11月4日至11月23日）
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 1922年11月26日破封时，卡特用蜡烛伸入洞口照明（因担心墓内可能有易燃气体，需先测试）
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》回忆

facts.content: 卡特回忆破封时'墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳'——3300年封闭空间的空气首次流通
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷

facts.content: 1925年10月28日开启最内层纯金棺盖，见到包裹中的木乃伊与黄金面具——距发现墓已近3年
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 帝王谷夏季地表温度可达50°C以上，1920年代无空调，工人与考古学家在帐篷与临时棚屋中工作
facts.source: 地理常识与卡特日记背景

facts.content: 1922年11月23日卡那封抵达后，团队用约1天时间（11月23-24日）清出全部16级台阶并露出封门
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 1922年11月4日早晨，一名当地工人在清理拉美西斯六世墓前的古代工棚地基时，铲子碰到了第一级石阶
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录（工人在场但姓名未留存于主流记录）

facts.slot: 最后一年资助的紧迫性
facts.content: 卡那封决定1922年为最后一年资助，若无发现将停止投资——这是卡特团队面临的最后期限压力
facts.source: 参考资料背景

facts.content: 1922年11月26日深夜四人秘密进入墓室（当时未公开），据卡特私人文件推测是为在官方开启前确认墓未被盗空
facts.source: 参考资料：依据卡特私人文件

facts.content: 1922年11月26日深夜秘密进入的四人：霍华德·卡特（考古学家）、阿瑟·卡伦德（助手）、卡那封伯爵、伊芙琳·赫伯特女士
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 图坦卡蒙死后被官方除名：霍伦海布时期系统性抹除阿玛尔纳时期法老的名字，后世王表（如阿拜多斯王表）中完全没有图坦卡蒙——这是他一度'在历史上查无此人'、墓未被系统盗掘的直接原因
facts.source: 参考资料古代文献

facts.content: 前厅中两尊与真人等大的法老守护者木雕像（黑色皮肤、镀金裙与头饰、手持权杖）分立通往墓室的封门两侧——卡特第一眼看到的'奇异的'形象
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单与卡特描述

facts.content: 1925年11月11-19日，卡特团队在KV15墓改建的临时实验室里揭开木乃伊裹布。木乃伊因大量树脂浇注粘连在金棺内，团队不得不用加热刀具分离。卡特日记记录：'这是必须做的工作，但每一刀都让人心痛'（意译，原文为对工作艰难性的描述）
facts.source: 参考资料：卡特1925年日记，The Griffith Institute档案

facts.slot: 木乃伊揭开时卡特情绪
facts.content: 卡特1925年日记记录揭开木乃伊瞬间：'非常整洁包裹的年轻国王木乃伊，戴着悲伤但平静表情的黄金面具，象征奥西里斯。图坦卡蒙的相似面容，在那墓葬的寂静中，让我们意识到过去'（原文：The similitude of the youthful Tut-ankh-Amen, until now known only by name, amid that sepulchral silence, made us realize the past）
facts.source: 卡特1925年9月日记，The Griffith Institute

facts.slot: 卡特对发现意义的反思
facts.content: 卡特日记记录：图坦卡蒙'也许是埋葬在那个皇家墓地的27人中最不重要的一位'，但他的墓因被遗忘而幸存，让现代人得以窥见古埃及葬礼的完整面貌
facts.source: 卡特日记，The Griffith Institute

facts.content: 1922年11月4日，帝王谷（Valley of the Kings），拉美西斯六世墓附近，当地工人在古代工棚遗迹下发现第一级石阶
facts.source: 霍华德·卡特著作《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷；卡特1922年11月6日致卡那封电报

facts.content: 卡特自1917年开始地毯式排查帝王谷，一战后连续数年一无所获；卡那封伯爵决定1922年为最后一年资助
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 卡特给英国卡那封发电报原文：'终于在帝王谷有了重大发现；一座封印完好的宏伟陵墓；已重新掩埋等候您到来；祝贺。'
facts.source: 卡特1922年11月6日电报，参考资料引用

facts.content: 1922年11月26日，卡特在第二道封门左上角凿开小洞，伸入蜡烛窥视。卡那封问：'你能看见什么吗？'卡特回答：'是的，美妙无比的东西。'（Yes, wonderful things.）
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷回忆原文

facts.content: 卡特回忆：'起初我什么也看不见，墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳。渐渐地，眼睛适应了光线，细节从朦胧中浮现——奇异的动物、雕像，还有黄金，到处都是黄金的闪光。'
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷

facts.content: 1922年11月26日深夜（当时未公开），卡特、助手卡伦德、卡那封与伊芙琳女士四人先行入内查看，成为3300多年来第一批进入墓室的现代人
facts.source: 参考资料：依据卡特私人文件，当时对外未承认

facts.content: 1922年11月29日在埃及官员与受邀贵宾见证下正式开墓
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 墓中登记文物5,398件，清理编目耗时约十年（1922-1932）
facts.source: 卡特编目记录，参考资料引用

facts.content: 黄金面具重10.23公斤纯金
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录（藏品号JE 60672）

facts.content: 最内层人形棺为110.4公斤纯金
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 1922年11月23日卡那封抵达后，清出全部16级台阶，封门上发现图坦卡蒙王名圈封印
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 封门上有古代打开并重新封堵的痕迹，证明下葬后不久遭两次盗掘，但被墓地官员及时重新封堵。学界估计约六成珠宝陪葬品已被盗走
facts.source: 参考资料考古记录与学界估计

facts.content: 约公元前12世纪，修建拉美西斯六世墓的工人在其正上方搭建工棚、倾倒碎石，入口被彻底覆盖
facts.source: 参考资料考古记录

facts.content: 前厅（卡特第一眼看到的房间）：镀金动物造型灵床、6辆拆解的战车、礼仪王座、储物箱；两尊与真人等大的法老守护者木雕像分立墓室封门两侧
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单

facts.content: 礼仪王座：木胎包金嵌银与彩陶；靠背为阿玛尔纳风格名画：王后安克赫娜蒙在太阳光芒下为法老涂抹香油。卡特称其为'迄今埃及出土最美之物'
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单，卡特评价

facts.content: 墓室是唯一有壁画的房间。北壁画继任者阿伊为法老主持'开口仪式'；西壁画12只狒狒（《杜阿特之书》第一时辰）。墙壁上有至今可见的褐色斑点——科学研究认为是封墓时灰泥与颜料未干、湿气滋生微生物所致，证明下葬极为仓促
facts.source: 参考资料与盖蒂保护研究所分析

facts.content: 卡特自1917年起在帝王谷地毯式排查，至1922年发现，坚持约5-6年
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 卡那封携女儿伊芙琳·赫伯特女士（Lady Evelyn Herbert）于1922年11月23日抵达卢克索，她是破封时在场的四人之一
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 木乃伊裹布中发现铁刃匕首（位于右腿侧，全长34.2厘米，金柄、水晶圆头）。2016年意大利团队用XRF检测：成分为铁+10.8%镍+0.58%钴，与陨铁特征高度吻合。铁在公元前14世纪的埃及比黄金珍贵
facts.source: 2016年《陨星学与行星科学》（Meteoritics & Planetary Science，DOI: 10.1111/maps.12664）

facts.content: 图坦卡蒙约公元前1332年登基（当时约9岁），约公元前1323年去世（约18-19岁），在位约9年
facts.source: 参考资料古代文献+科学研究综合

facts.content: 从图坦卡蒙下葬（约公元前1323年）到1922年开启，墓封存约3245年
facts.method: 1323 + 1922 = 3245年（跨公元0年无需减1，因公元前1年后是公元1年）

facts.content: 四层镀金木神龛层层套在石棺之外，最外层大到几乎填满墓室
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单

facts.content: 1924年2月卡特因不满埃及政府监管宣布'罢工'辞职；1925年1月在新协议下复工（全部文物归埃及，不再分成）。1932年清理完毕。1939年3月2日卡特病逝于伦敦，终年64岁
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.slot: 卡那封之死与诅咒辟谣
facts.content: 1923年4月5日卡那封伯爵死于开罗（面颊蚊虫叮咬感染发展为败血症），终年56岁。2002年《英国医学杂志》研究：对比44名西方人，25人'暴露组'平均死亡年龄70岁，未暴露组75岁，校正后无统计学差异。卡特本人又活了17年至64岁
facts.source: 2002年12月《英国医学杂志》（BMJ），澳大利亚莫纳什大学马克·尼尔森研究

facts.content: 1920年代帝王谷考古营地条件：沙漠高温、无现代设施、需从尼罗河运水、帐篷营地、煤油灯照明
facts.source: 参考资料背景与卡特日记记载

facts.content: 当地埃及工人是1922年11月4日发现第一级石阶的直接发现者；发掘团队雇佣大量当地劳工进行挖掘与搬运
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 1922年11月4日发现台阶后，卡特立即发电报并重新掩埋现场，等待卡那封从英国赶来，等待时间约19天（11月4日至11月23日）
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 1922年11月26日破封时，卡特用蜡烛伸入洞口照明（因担心墓内可能有易燃气体，需先测试）
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》回忆

facts.content: 卡特回忆破封时'墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳'——3300年封闭空间的空气首次流通
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷

facts.content: 1925年10月28日开启最内层纯金棺盖，见到包裹中的木乃伊与黄金面具——距发现墓已近3年
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 帝王谷夏季地表温度可达50°C以上，1920年代无空调，工人与考古学家在帐篷与临时棚屋中工作
facts.source: 地理常识与卡特日记背景

candidates.text: 1922年11月4日，埃及帝王谷。我的铲子碰到了一块石头。不是普通的石头——是一级台阶。下面埋着一座被遗忘3000年的法老陵墓，里面有110公斤纯金。但那天早上，我只是一个拿着一天工资的工人。（F01+F33+F10+F21）
1922年11月26日，埃及。我站在一扇封了3300年的门前。考古学家卡特凿开一个小洞，伸进一根蜡烛。他身后的伯爵问：'你能看见什么吗？'卡特回答：'是的，美妙无比的东西。'三天前，是我第一个发现这座墓的入口。（F04+F05+F21+F33）
1922年，埃及。我们在沙漠里挖了6年，什么也没找到。资助人说这是最后一年。11月4日早上，我的铲子碰到了一级台阶。下面是图坦卡蒙的墓——唯一没被盗空的法老陵墓，5398件文物，10公斤黄金面具。但那一刻，我们谁也不知道。（F02+F17+F34+F01+F33+F08+F09）

facts.content: 1922年11月4日，帝王谷（Valley of the Kings），拉美西斯六世墓附近，当地工人在古代工棚遗迹下发现第一级石阶
facts.source: 霍华德·卡特著作《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷；卡特1922年11月6日致卡那封电报

facts.content: 卡特自1917年开始地毯式排查帝王谷，一战后连续数年一无所获；卡那封伯爵决定1922年为最后一年资助
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 卡特给英国卡那封发电报原文：'终于在帝王谷有了重大发现；一座封印完好的宏伟陵墓；已重新掩埋等候您到来；祝贺。'
facts.source: 卡特1922年11月6日电报，参考资料引用

facts.content: 1922年11月26日，卡特在第二道封门左上角凿开小洞，伸入蜡烛窥视。卡那封问：'你能看见什么吗？'卡特回答：'是的，美妙无比的东西。'（Yes, wonderful things.）
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷回忆原文

facts.content: 卡特回忆：'起初我什么也看不见，墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳。渐渐地，眼睛适应了光线，细节从朦胧中浮现——奇异的动物、雕像，还有黄金，到处都是黄金的闪光。'
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷

facts.content: 1922年11月26日深夜（当时未公开），卡特、助手卡伦德、卡那封与伊芙琳女士四人先行入内查看，成为3300多年来第一批进入墓室的现代人
facts.source: 参考资料：依据卡特私人文件，当时对外未承认

facts.content: 1922年11月29日在埃及官员与受邀贵宾见证下正式开墓
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 墓中登记文物5,398件，清理编目耗时约十年（1922-1932）
facts.source: 卡特编目记录，参考资料引用

facts.content: 黄金面具重10.23公斤纯金
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录（藏品号JE 60672）

facts.content: 最内层人形棺为110.4公斤纯金
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 1922年11月23日卡那封抵达后，清出全部16级台阶，封门上发现图坦卡蒙王名圈封印
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 封门上有古代打开并重新封堵的痕迹，证明下葬后不久遭两次盗掘，但被墓地官员及时重新封堵。学界估计约六成珠宝陪葬品已被盗走
facts.source: 参考资料考古记录与学界估计

facts.content: 约公元前12世纪，修建拉美西斯六世墓的工人在其正上方搭建工棚、倾倒碎石，入口被彻底覆盖
facts.source: 参考资料考古记录

facts.content: 前厅（卡特第一眼看到的房间）：镀金动物造型灵床、6辆拆解的战车、礼仪王座、储物箱；两尊与真人等大的法老守护者木雕像分立墓室封门两侧
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单

facts.content: 礼仪王座：木胎包金嵌银与彩陶；靠背为阿玛尔纳风格名画：王后安克赫娜蒙在太阳光芒下为法老涂抹香油。卡特称其为'迄今埃及出土最美之物'
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单，卡特评价

facts.content: 墓室是唯一有壁画的房间。北壁画继任者阿伊为法老主持'开口仪式'；西壁画12只狒狒（《杜阿特之书》第一时辰）。墙壁上有至今可见的褐色斑点——科学研究认为是封墓时灰泥与颜料未干、湿气滋生微生物所致，证明下葬极为仓促
facts.source: 参考资料与盖蒂保护研究所分析

facts.content: 卡特自1917年起在帝王谷地毯式排查，至1922年发现，坚持约5-6年
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 卡那封携女儿伊芙琳·赫伯特女士（Lady Evelyn Herbert）于1922年11月23日抵达卢克索，她是破封时在场的四人之一
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 木乃伊裹布中发现铁刃匕首（位于右腿侧，全长34.2厘米，金柄、水晶圆头）。2016年意大利团队用XRF检测：成分为铁+10.8%镍+0.58%钴，与陨铁特征高度吻合。铁在公元前14世纪的埃及比黄金珍贵
facts.source: 2016年《陨星学与行星科学》（Meteoritics & Planetary Science，DOI: 10.1111/maps.12664）

facts.content: 图坦卡蒙约公元前1332年登基（当时约9岁），约公元前1323年去世（约18-19岁），在位约9年
facts.source: 参考资料古代文献+科学研究综合

facts.content: 从图坦卡蒙下葬（约公元前1323年）到1922年开启，墓封存约3245年
facts.method: 1323 + 1922 = 3245年（跨公元0年无需减1，因公元前1年后是公元1年）

facts.content: 四层镀金木神龛层层套在石棺之外，最外层大到几乎填满墓室
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单

facts.content: 1924年2月卡特因不满埃及政府监管宣布'罢工'辞职；1925年1月在新协议下复工（全部文物归埃及，不再分成）。1932年清理完毕。1939年3月2日卡特病逝于伦敦，终年64岁
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.slot: 卡那封之死与诅咒辟谣
facts.content: 1923年4月5日卡那封伯爵死于开罗（面颊蚊虫叮咬感染发展为败血症），终年56岁。2002年《英国医学杂志》研究：对比44名西方人，25人'暴露组'平均死亡年龄70岁，未暴露组75岁，校正后无统计学差异。卡特本人又活了17年至64岁
facts.source: 2002年12月《英国医学杂志》（BMJ），澳大利亚莫纳什大学马克·尼尔森研究

facts.content: 1920年代帝王谷考古营地条件：沙漠高温、无现代设施、需从尼罗河运水、帐篷营地、煤油灯照明
facts.source: 参考资料背景与卡特日记记载

facts.content: 当地埃及工人是1922年11月4日发现第一级石阶的直接发现者；发掘团队雇佣大量当地劳工进行挖掘与搬运
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 1922年11月4日发现台阶后，卡特立即发电报并重新掩埋现场，等待卡那封从英国赶来，等待时间约19天（11月4日至11月23日）
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 1922年11月26日破封时，卡特用蜡烛伸入洞口照明（因担心墓内可能有易燃气体，需先测试）
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》回忆

facts.content: 卡特回忆破封时'墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳'——3300年封闭空间的空气首次流通
facts.source: 卡特《图坦卡蒙墓》第一卷

facts.content: 1925年10月28日开启最内层纯金棺盖，见到包裹中的木乃伊与黄金面具——距发现墓已近3年
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 帝王谷夏季地表温度可达50°C以上，1920年代无空调，工人与考古学家在帐篷与临时棚屋中工作
facts.source: 地理常识与卡特日记背景

facts.content: 1922年11月23日卡那封抵达后，团队用约1天时间（11月23-24日）清出全部16级台阶并露出封门
facts.source: 参考资料时间线

facts.content: 1922年11月4日早晨，一名当地工人在清理拉美西斯六世墓前的古代工棚地基时，铲子碰到了第一级石阶
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录（工人在场但姓名未留存于主流记录）

facts.slot: 最后一年资助的紧迫性
facts.content: 卡那封决定1922年为最后一年资助，若无发现将停止投资——这是卡特团队面临的最后期限压力
facts.source: 参考资料背景

facts.content: 1922年11月26日深夜四人秘密进入墓室（当时未公开），据卡特私人文件推测是为在官方开启前确认墓未被盗空
facts.source: 参考资料：依据卡特私人文件

facts.content: 1922年11月26日深夜秘密进入的四人：霍华德·卡特（考古学家）、阿瑟·卡伦德（助手）、卡那封伯爵、伊芙琳·赫伯特女士
facts.source: 参考资料档案记录

facts.content: 图坦卡蒙死后被官方除名：霍伦海布时期系统性抹除阿玛尔纳时期法老的名字，后世王表（如阿拜多斯王表）中完全没有图坦卡蒙——这是他一度'在历史上查无此人'、墓未被系统盗掘的直接原因
facts.source: 参考资料古代文献

facts.content: 前厅中两尊与真人等大的法老守护者木雕像（黑色皮肤、镀金裙与头饰、手持权杖）分立通往墓室的封门两侧——卡特第一眼看到的'奇异的'形象
facts.source: 参考资料文物清单与卡特描述

# I Was the Worker Who Opened Tutankhamun's Tomb - Full Script

---

[CH01 | 0:00-0:20 | immersive_premise_hook]

November 4th, 1922. Valley of the Kings, Egypt. My shovel hits a stone. Not just any stone. A step. There's something underneath. A tomb that's been forgotten for 3,000 years. Inside, 110 kilograms of pure gold. But this morning, I'm just a worker getting paid by the day.

---

[CH02 | 0:20-0:34 | authenticity_contract]

Everything you're about to see comes from Howard Carter's own book, archive photographs, and site records from 1922. This is as close as we can get to what it was actually like to be there. To be the first person in over three millennia to see what's inside.

---

[CH03 | 0:34-0:52 | mission_briefing]

Okay, just between you and me, we're here to do two things. First, prove this isn't another looted tomb. The ancient thieves got into almost every other one. Second, witness the moment Carter breaks that seal. The moment he sees what's been sealed since 1323 BC. We're going in.

---

[CH04 | 0:52-1:25 | threshold_crossing]

Every morning starts the same. Sunrise over the Valley. We gather at the camp, tents and oil lamps, no running water. Carter walks through, checks yesterday's progress. He speaks some Arabic, we speak some English, mostly we point. It's 50 degrees Celsius by noon. We've been digging here for six years. Found nothing. But today, when I hit that step, Carter drops to his knees. He's not checking the hole. He's staring at it. That's when I know. This time is different.

---

[CH05 | 1:25-2:35 | daily_life_exploration]

Now we wait. Carter sends a telegram to England: "At last have made wonderful discovery in Valley; a magnificent tomb with seals intact; re-covered same for your arrival; congratulations." He buries it again. For 19 days, we cover the steps every single evening. If word gets out, tomb robbers will come. So every night, sand goes back on. Every morning, we uncover it again, make sure it's still there. It's still there. The desert doesn't change. We haul water from the Nile. We eat the same flat bread and lentils. I sleep in a tent that smells like canvas and dust. I've stayed in worse places. At night, it's actually cold. During the day, the sand is too hot to touch with bare hands. We move stones, we carry baskets, we wait. Nineteen days of knowing there's a tomb right under our feet and we can't look inside.

---

[CH06 | 2:35-4:34 | steerage_social_life]

You have to understand, Carter's been looking since 1917. Five years of digging, grid by grid, finding nothing. His sponsor, Lord Carnarvon, told him this is the last year. No discovery, no more money. That's the deadline hanging over all of us. And now, we found it. Carnarvon's sailing from England with his daughter, Lady Evelyn Herbert. She's 20 years old, keeps a camera, takes notes. The British call her a "lady." She calls herself lucky. I work next to a man named Ahmed. He's got three kids. He tells me he's saving for a donkey so his son can sell vegetables in Luxor instead of digging. "What do you think is down there?" he asks. I tell him, gold. Maybe. He says, "Even if there's nothing, we were the ones who found the door." That's all he wants. To have found the door. I don't tell him I hope there's more. Carnarvon arrives in 19 days. Tonight, we'll clear all the steps.

---

[CH07 | 4:34-5:53 | communal_celebration]

November 4th, 1922, morning. I'm clearing rubble from in front of Ramesses VI's tomb. There used to be workers' huts here, 3,000 years ago. We're taking them apart, stone by stone. My shovel goes in. It hits something flat. Not a rock. I call Carter. He comes over, kneels down, brushes sand with his hands. A cut stone. A step. We keep going. One step. Two. By noon, we've uncovered twelve. It's a staircase going down. Carter finds a seal on the doorway at the bottom. He can read the hieroglyphs. He looks up. "This is a tomb." Not a storage room. Not a cache. A tomb. Nobody says anything. Ahmed grips my shoulder. We're all just standing there, staring at a doorway that's been buried since before anyone can remember. Carter's smiling. I've never seen him smile.

---

[CH08 | 5:53-7:10 | confession_and_heist]

Here's the thing. You already know what's inside. I didn't. For 19 days, we didn't know. See, there are signs of ancient break-ins on that sealed door. Robbers got in twice, maybe 3,200 years ago, right after the burial. The necropolis officials sealed it back up, but we don't know how much they took. Every other royal tomb in this valley has been stripped clean. So for 19 days, we're working on a question: is this going to be another empty room? Carter reburies the stairs. We cover them with sand and stones every night. During the day, we sit in camp and wait. Ahmed asks, "What if it's empty?" I don't answer. I don't know.

---

[CH09 | 7:10-8:25 | forbidden_luxury_reveal]

November 26th, 1922. Carnarvon's here. We've cleared all sixteen steps. There's a doorway, sealed, with Tutankhamun's name on it. Carter makes a small hole in the top left corner. He lights a candle, reaches in. Carnarvon asks, "Can you see anything?" Carter's silent for a moment. Then, "Yes, wonderful things." Here's what he wrote later: "At first I could see nothing, the hot air escaping from the chamber causing the candle flame to flicker, but presently, as my eyes grew accustomed to the light, details of the room within emerged slowly from the mist, strange animals, statues, and gold. Everywhere the glint of gold." That night, November 26th, four people go in. Carter, his assistant Callender, Carnarvon, and Evelyn. They don't tell anyone. They're the first people in 3,300 years to step inside.

---

[CH10 | 8:25-9:19 | luxury_catalog]

The front room. Six chariots, disassembled. Three golden beds shaped like animals. A throne covered in gold and silver, with a painting of the queen anointing the king. Carter calls it the most beautiful object ever found in Egypt. Boxes. Statues. Two life-sized figures of the pharaoh in black and gold, standing guard on either side of the sealed burial chamber door. Beyond that, four nested shrines covered in gold, so large they almost fill the room. Inside those, a stone sarcophagus. Inside that, three coffins. The innermost coffin: 110.4 kilograms of solid gold. The mask on the mummy's face: 10.23 kilograms. In total, 5,398 objects. They'll spend ten years cataloging everything.

---

[CH11 | 9:19-9:55 | dramatic_irony_turn]

But here's what nobody's saying yet. This isn't just treasure. This is a person. Tutankhamun was about 18 years old when he died, around 1323 BC. He ruled for nine years, starting when he was a child. After his death, his name was erased from the official king lists. Later pharaohs pretended he never existed. That's why this tomb survived. Nobody remembered it was here. And the burial was rushed. You can see it in the tomb paintings, brown spots on the wet plaster where mold grew because they sealed it before the paint dried. He was forgotten for 3,245 years.

---

[CH12 | 9:55-10:50 | plan_rehearsal]

Opening the tomb takes ten years. November 1922, we find the steps. February 1923, we open the burial chamber. But the shrines are nested so tightly, they have to be disassembled panel by panel. 1924, Carter walks off the job. The Egyptian government wants control. He refuses. They shut down the dig. 1925, he comes back under a new agreement: everything stays in Egypt. October 28th, 1925, they finally open the innermost golden coffin. That's three years after we found the door. Inside, the mummy is completely stuck to the coffin with resin. They have to use heated knives to separate the wrappings. It takes until 1932 to remove and catalog every single object.

---

[CH13 | 10:50-11:25 | futile_warning]

Carter writes in his diary, November 1925: the work is necessary, but every cut feels wrong. They're unwrapping a body that was wrapped 3,300 years ago. The resin has turned solid. The linen is fused to the gold. He writes, "The youthful likeness of Tut-ankh-Amen made us realize the past." This isn't just archaeology. This is touching someone who was buried with care, in a hurry, by people who thought he'd rest undisturbed forever. And here we are, cutting him free.

---

[CH14 | 11:25-12:21 | countdown_and_impact]

October 28th, 1925. They lift the lid of the innermost coffin. The mummy is wrapped in linen. Layer after layer. They peel it back slowly. And then, there it is. The golden mask. 10.23 kilograms of gold, inlaid with blue glass and semi-precious stones. The face of an 18-year-old king. The eyes are open. They're looking at you. Right now, across 3,245 years, his eyes are looking at the people who opened his tomb. You are standing in 1925, staring at 1323 BC. That's the moment. That's what it means to be first.

---

[CH15 | 12:21-13:17 | collapse_witnessing]

April 5th, 1923. Six months after the discovery, Lord Carnarvon dies in Cairo. A mosquito bite on his cheek, infected, turned to blood poisoning. He's 56. The newspapers call it the curse of the pharaohs. In 2002, the British Medical Journal does a study: 25 people present at the opening, average age at death 70 years. No statistical difference from the unexposed group. But the story sticks. Carter keeps working. He fights with officials, walks out, comes back. 1932, the tomb is finally empty. 1939, Carter dies in London. He's 64. Seventeen years after he opened the tomb.

---

[CH16 | 13:17-15:00 | closure_reflection]

November 4th, 1922. My shovel hits a step. I call Carter. We uncover a doorway. For 19 days, we don't know if there's anything inside. November 26th, Carter makes a hole, lights a candle, and says, "Wonderful things." I'm there. Not in the room, but outside, waiting. Ahmed's next to me. Evelyn's taking photographs. Carnarvon's leaning over Carter's shoulder. We are the first people in 3,245 years to know this tomb exists. The books will say "Tutankhamun's tomb was discovered in 1922." That's true. But it's one thing to read about a discovery. It's another thing to be standing there, in the Valley, in the heat, not knowing what's below, and then seeing gold shine back at you from the dark. The past isn't a story. It's a room you can walk into, if you're the one holding the candle. And for a moment, just a moment, time stops.

# I Was the Worker Who Opened Tutankhamun's Tomb - Optimized Script

November 4th, 1922. Valley of the Kings, Egypt. My shovel hits stone. Not just any stone. A step. Something buried underneath. A tomb forgotten for 3,244 years. Inside, over 110 kilograms of solid gold. But right now, I'm just a worker getting paid by the day.

He's not checking the hole. He's staring. That's when I know. This time is different.

---

Ahmed asks me at night: "What if it's empty?" I don't answer. Nobody does. Nineteen days of knowing there's a tomb under our feet. We can't look inside.

---

[CH06 | 2:35-4:34 | steerage_social_life]

Ahmed tells me this is Carter's last season. His sponsor—some English lord—won't pay for another year. That's why Carter walks the site every evening. Checking. Measuring. He's running out of time. ---

Carter's standing there. He's smiling. Crying. I've never seen him smile. Then he stops. Looks at each of us. His voice drops: "Tonight we cover it. Tell no one. [CH08 | 5:53-7:10 | confession_and_heist]

November 11th, 1925. KV15 tomb, converted into a laboratory. The golden coffin is open. Inside, the mummy, wrapped in linen, covered in black resin. Hardened. Fused to the gold. Every layer of linen is someone's prayer. And we're tearing it open.

[CH14 | 11:25-12:21 | countdown_and_impact]

November 19th, 1925. The last layer. Carter's hands are shaking. He grips the edge of the linen. Pulls. Slowly. The fabric resists. Then gives. Gold. Just a sliver at first. Then more. The edge of a headdress. A curve. Carter stops. Takes a breath. Pulls again. The mask emerges. 10.23 kilograms of solid gold. Inlaid with blue glass and lapis lazuli. Everyone steps back. As if pushed. The room goes silent. No camera clicks. No breathing. Just the mask. And then I see them. The eyes. Inlaid. Staring straight ahead. Open. They're looking at you. Not past you. At you. November 4th, 1922. My shovel hits a step. I call Carter. We uncover a doorway. For 19 days, we don't know if there's anything inside. November 26th, Carter makes a hole, lights a candle, and says, "Wonderful things." I'm there. Not in the room, but outside. Waiting. Ahmed's next to me. November 19th, 1925. The last layer of linen pulled away. The mask staring back. The room goes silent. Ahmed drops to his knees. That's when time stops. Not because the clock stops. Because you realize you're standing at the edge of 3,000 years. On one side, 1925. On the other, 1323 BC. And between them, just you. Holding a candle. Looking into his eyes. Ahmed bought his donkey in 1926. His son sells vegetables in Luxor market now. Sometimes he points at the museum and tells tourists: my father found that tomb. That's all he wanted. He buries it again. For 19 days, we cover the steps every single evening. If word gets out, tomb robbers come. So every night, sand goes back on. Every morning, we uncover it again. Make sure it's still there. It's still there. The desert doesn't change. We haul water from the Nile. Eat the same flatbread. Same lentils. I sleep in a tent that smells like canvas and dust. I've stayed in worse places. At night, it's cold. During the day, sand too hot to touch bare-handed. We move stones. Carry baskets. Wait. Nineteen days of knowing there's a tomb right under our feet. Can't look inside.

---

[CH06 | 2:35-4:34 | steerage_social_life]

You have to understand. Carter's been looking since 1917. Six years of digging, grid by grid, finding nothing. His sponsor, Lord Carnarvon, had told him: 1922 is the last year. No discovery, no more money. That deadline hangs over all of us. And now, we found it. Carnarvon's sailing from England with his daughter, Lady Evelyn Herbert. She's 20 years old. Keeps a camera. Takes notes. The British call her a "lady." She calls herself lucky. I work next to a man named Ahmed. Three kids. He's saving for a donkey so his son can sell vegetables in Luxor instead of digging. "What do you think is down there?" he asks. I tell him, gold. Maybe. He says, "Even if there's nothing, we were the ones who found the door." That's all he wants. To have found the door. I don't tell him I hope there's more. I watch Carter pace the site every evening. He measures the steps again. Checks the seal. Walks away. Comes back. Carnarvon arrives in 19 days. Tonight, we clear all the steps.

---

[CH07 | 4:34-5:53 | communal_celebration]

November 4th, 1922, morning. I'm clearing rubble from in front of Ramesses VI's tomb. There used to be workers' huts here, 3,000 years ago. We're taking them apart, stone by stone. My shovel goes in. Hits something flat. Not a rock. I call Carter. He comes over. Kneels down. Brushes sand with his hands. A cut stone. A step. We keep going. One step. Two. By noon, we've uncovered twelve. It's a staircase going down. Carter finds a seal on the doorway at the bottom. He can read the hieroglyphs. He looks up. "This is a tomb." Not a storage room. Not a cache. A tomb. Nobody says anything. Ahmed grips my shoulder. We stand there. Staring at a doorway buried since before anyone can remember. Carter's smiling. I've never seen him smile. He stands. Brushes off his knees. Looks at each of us. "We cover it tonight. Tell no one."

---

[CH08 | 5:53-7:10 | confession_and_heist]

Here's the thing. You already know what's inside. I didn't. For 19 days, we didn't know. See, there are signs of ancient break-ins on that sealed door. Robbers got in twice, maybe 3,200 years ago. Right after the burial. The necropolis officials sealed it back up. But we don't know how much they took. Every other royal tomb in this valley has been stripped clean. So for 19 days, we're working on a question: is this another empty room? Carter reburies the stairs. We cover them with sand and stones every night. During the day, we sit in camp. Wait. Ahmed asks, "What if it's empty?" I don't answer. None of us do.

---

[CH09 | 7:10-8:25 | forbidden_luxury_reveal]

November 26th, 1922. Carnarvon's here. We've cleared all sixteen steps. There's a doorway, sealed, with Tutankhamun's name on it. Carter makes a small hole in the top left corner. He lights a candle first—testing for dangerous gases—then reaches in. Carnarvon asks, "Can you see anything?" Carter's silent for a moment. Then: "Yes, wonderful things." Here's what he wrote later: "At first I could see nothing, the hot air escaping from the chamber causing the candle flame to flicker, but presently, as my eyes grew accustomed to the light, details of the room within emerged slowly from the mist, strange animals, statues, and gold. Everywhere the glint of gold." That night, November 26th, four people go in. Carter. His assistant Callender. Carnarvon. Evelyn. They don't tell anyone. They're the first people in 3,300 years to step inside.

---

[CH10 | 8:25-9:19 | luxury_catalog]

The front room. Six chariots, disassembled. Three golden beds shaped like animals. A throne covered in gold and silver, with a painting of the queen anointing the king. Carter calls it the most beautiful object ever found in Egypt. Boxes. Statues. Two life-sized figures of the pharaoh in black and gold, standing guard on either side of the sealed burial chamber door. Beyond that, four nested shrines covered in gold, so large they almost fill the room. Inside those, a stone sarcophagus. Inside that, three coffins. The innermost coffin: 110.4 kilograms of solid gold. The mask on the mummy's face: 10.23 kilograms. In total, 5,398 objects. They'll spend ten years cataloging everything.

---

[CH11 | 9:19-9:55 | dramatic_irony_turn]

But here's what nobody's saying yet. This isn't just treasure. This is a person. Tutankhamun was about 18 years old when he died, around 1323 BC. He ruled for nine years, starting when he was a child. After his death, his name was erased. Official king lists. Later pharaohs pretended he never existed. That's why this tomb survived. Nobody remembered it was here. The burial was rushed. You can see it in the tomb paintings. Brown spots on the wet plaster. Mold grew because they sealed it before the paint dried. Based on documented dates, he was forgotten for 3,245 years.

---

[CH12 | 9:55-10:50 | plan_rehearsal]

Opening the tomb takes ten years. November 1922, we find the steps. February 1923, we open the burial chamber. But the shrines are nested so tightly, they have to be disassembled panel by panel. 1924, Carter walks off the job. The Egyptian government wants control. He refuses. They shut down the dig. 1925, he comes back under a new agreement: everything stays in Egypt. October 28th, 1925, they finally open the innermost golden coffin. That's three years just to reach the innermost coffin. The full excavation takes ten years, until 1932.

---

[CH13 | 10:50-11:25 | futile_warning]

October 1925. Carter opens the innermost coffin. The mummy is completely stuck to the coffin with resin. They have to use heated knives to separate the wrappings. November 11th to 19th, in a temporary laboratory, they unwrap a body wrapped 3,300 years ago. The resin has turned solid. The linen is fused to the gold. Carter writes in his diary: the work is necessary, but every cut feels wrong. "The youthful likeness of Tut-ankh-Amen made us realize the past." This isn't just archaeology. This is touching someone who was buried with care, in a hurry, by people who thought he'd rest undisturbed forever. And here we are. Cutting him free.

---

[CH14 | 11:25-12:21 | countdown_and_impact]

October 28th, 1925. They lift the lid of the innermost coffin. The mummy is wrapped in linen. Layer after layer. They peel it back slowly. Then, there it is. The golden mask. 10.23 kilograms of gold. Inlaid with blue glass and semi-precious stones. The face of an 18-year-old king. The eyes are open. They're looking at you. Right now, across 3,245 years, his eyes are looking at the people who opened his tomb. You are standing in 1925, staring at 1323 BC. That's the moment. That's what it means to be first.

---

[CH15 | 12:21-13:17 | collapse_witnessing]

April 5th, 1923. Six months after the discovery. Lord Carnarvon dies in Cairo. A mosquito bite on his cheek. Infected. Turned to blood poisoning. He's 56. The newspapers call it the curse of the pharaohs. 2002, the British Medical Journal does a study. 44 Westerners connected to the excavation. 25 in the exposed group. Average age at death: 70 years. 19 in the unexposed group. Average: 75 years. After adjustment, no statistical difference. But the story sticks. Carter keeps working. He fights with officials. Walks out. Comes back. 1932, the tomb is finally empty. 1939, Carter dies in London. He's 64. Seventeen years after he opened the tomb.

---

[CH16 | 13:17-15:00 | closure_reflection]

November 4th, 1922. My shovel hits a step. I call Carter. We uncover a doorway. For 19 days, we don't know if there's anything inside. November 26th, Carter makes a hole, lights a candle, and says, "Wonderful things." I'm there. Not in the room, but outside. Waiting. Ahmed's next to me. Evelyn's taking photographs. Carnarvon's leaning over Carter's shoulder. We are the first people in 3,245 years to know this tomb exists. The books will say "Tutankhamun's tomb was discovered in 1922." That's true. But it's one thing to read about a discovery. It's another thing to be standing there, in the Valley, in the heat, not knowing what's below, and then seeing gold shine back at you from the dark. The past isn't a story. It's a room you can walk into, if you're the one holding the candle. That's when time stops.

stale_facts.content: 1922年11月4日，帝王谷（Valley of the Kings），拉美西斯六世墓附近，当地工人在古代工棚遗迹下发现第一级石阶
卡特自1917年开始地毯式排查帝王谷，一战后连续数年一无所获；卡那封伯爵决定1922年为最后一年资助
卡特给英国卡那封发电报原文：'终于在帝王谷有了重大发现；一座封印完好的宏伟陵墓；已重新掩埋等候您到来；祝贺。'
1922年11月26日，卡特在第二道封门左上角凿开小洞，伸入蜡烛窥视。卡那封问：'你能看见什么吗？'卡特回答：'是的，美妙无比的东西。'（Yes, wonderful things.）
卡特回忆：'起初我什么也看不见，墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳。渐渐地，眼睛适应了光线，细节从朦胧中浮现——奇异的动物、雕像，还有黄金，到处都是黄金的闪光。'
1922年11月26日深夜（当时未公开），卡特、助手卡伦德、卡那封与伊芙琳女士四人先行入内查看，成为3300多年来第一批进入墓室的现代人
1922年11月29日在埃及官员与受邀贵宾见证下正式开墓
墓中登记文物5,398件，清理编目耗时约十年（1922-1932）
黄金面具重10.23公斤纯金
最内层人形棺为110.4公斤纯金
1922年11月23日卡那封抵达后，清出全部16级台阶，封门上发现图坦卡蒙王名圈封印
封门上有古代打开并重新封堵的痕迹，证明下葬后不久遭两次盗掘，但被墓地官员及时重新封堵。学界估计约六成珠宝陪葬品已被盗走
前厅（卡特第一眼看到的房间）：镀金动物造型灵床、6辆拆解的战车、礼仪王座、储物箱；两尊与真人等大的法老守护者木雕像分立墓室封门两侧
礼仪王座：木胎包金嵌银与彩陶；靠背为阿玛尔纳风格名画：王后安克赫娜蒙在太阳光芒下为法老涂抹香油。卡特称其为'迄今埃及出土最美之物'
墓室是唯一有壁画的房间。北壁画继任者阿伊为法老主持'开口仪式'；西壁画12只狒狒（《杜阿特之书》第一时辰）。墙壁上有至今可见的褐色斑点——科学研究认为是封墓时灰泥与颜料未干、湿气滋生微生物所致，证明下葬极为仓促
卡特自1917年起在帝王谷地毯式排查，至1922年发现，坚持约5-6年
卡那封携女儿伊芙琳·赫伯特女士（Lady Evelyn Herbert）于1922年11月23日抵达卢克索，她是破封时在场的四人之一
木乃伊裹布中发现铁刃匕首（位于右腿侧，全长34.2厘米，金柄、水晶圆头）。2016年意大利团队用XRF检测：成分为铁+10.8%镍+0.58%钴，与陨铁特征高度吻合。铁在公元前14世纪的埃及比黄金珍贵
图坦卡蒙约公元前1332年登基（当时约9岁），约公元前1323年去世（约18-19岁），在位约9年
从图坦卡蒙下葬（约公元前1323年）到1922年开启，墓封存约3245年
四层镀金木神龛层层套在石棺之外，最外层大到几乎填满墓室
1924年2月卡特因不满埃及政府监管宣布'罢工'辞职；1925年1月在新协议下复工（全部文物归埃及，不再分成）。1932年清理完毕。1939年3月2日卡特病逝于伦敦，终年64岁
1923年4月5日卡那封伯爵死于开罗（面颊蚊虫叮咬感染发展为败血症），终年56岁。2002年《英国医学杂志》研究：对比44名西方人，25人'暴露组'平均死亡年龄70岁，未暴露组75岁，校正后无统计学差异。卡特本人又活了17年至64岁
1920年代帝王谷考古营地条件：沙漠高温、无现代设施、需从尼罗河运水、帐篷营地、煤油灯照明
当地埃及工人是1922年11月4日发现第一级石阶的直接发现者；发掘团队雇佣大量当地劳工进行挖掘与搬运
1922年11月4日发现台阶后，卡特立即发电报并重新掩埋现场，等待卡那封从英国赶来，等待时间约19天（11月4日至11月23日）
1922年11月26日破封时，卡特用蜡烛伸入洞口照明（因担心墓内可能有易燃气体，需先测试）
卡特回忆破封时'墓室里涌出的热气吹得烛光摇曳'——3300年封闭空间的空气首次流通
1925年10月28日开启最内层纯金棺盖，见到包裹中的木乃伊与黄金面具——距发现墓已近3年
帝王谷夏季地表温度可达50°C以上，1920年代无空调，工人与考古学家在帐篷与临时棚屋中工作
1922年11月23日卡那封抵达后，团队用约1天时间（11月23-24日）清出全部16级台阶并露出封门
1922年11月4日早晨，一名当地工人在清理拉美西斯六世墓前的古代工棚地基时，铲子碰到了第一级石阶
卡那封决定1922年为最后一年资助，若无发现将停止投资——这是卡特团队面临的最后期限压力
1922年11月26日深夜四人秘密进入墓室（当时未公开），据卡特私人文件推测是为在官方开启前确认墓未被盗空
1922年11月26日深夜秘密进入的四人：霍华德·卡特（考古学家）、阿瑟·卡伦德（助手）、卡那封伯爵、伊芙琳·赫伯特女士
前厅中两尊与真人等大的法老守护者木雕像（黑色皮肤、镀金裙与头饰、手持权杖）分立通往墓室的封门两侧——卡特第一眼看到的'奇异的'形象
1925年11月11-19日，卡特团队在KV15墓改建的临时实验室里揭开木乃伊裹布。木乃伊因大量树脂浇注粘连在金棺内，团队不得不用加热刀具分离。卡特日记记录：'这是必须做的工作，但每一刀都让人心痛'（意译，原文为对工作艰难性的描述）

卡特1925年日记记录揭开木乃伊瞬间：'非常整洁包裹的年轻国王木乃伊，戴着悲伤但平静表情的黄金面具，象征奥西里斯。图坦卡蒙的相似面容，在那墓葬的寂静中，让我们意识到过去'（原文：The similitude of the youthful Tut-ankh-Amen, until now known only by name, amid that sepulchral silence, made us realize the past）
卡特日记记录：图坦卡蒙'也许是埋葬在那个皇家墓地的27人中最不重要的一位'，但他的墓因被遗忘而幸存，让现代人得以窥见古埃及葬礼的完整面貌

# I Was the Worker Who Opened Tutankhamun's Tomb - Optimized Script
[CH01 | 0:00-0:20 | immersive_premise_hook]

November 4th, 1922. Valley of the Kings, Egypt. My shovel hits stone. Not just any stone. A step. Something buried underneath. A tomb forgotten for 3,245 years. Inside, 110 kilograms of solid gold. But right now, I'm just a worker getting paid by the day.

---

[CH02 | 0:20-0:34 | authenticity_contract]

What you're about to see comes from Howard Carter's own book, archive photographs, and 1922 site records. We've reconstructed it as accurately as possible. What it was actually like to be there. To be the first person in over three millennia to see what's inside.

---

[CH03 | 0:34-0:52 | mission_briefing]

Okay, just between you and me. We're here to do two things. First, prove this isn't another looted tomb. Ancient thieves got into almost every other one. Second, witness the moment Carter breaks that seal. The moment he sees what's been sealed since 1323 BC. Let's go in.

---

[CH04 | 0:52-1:25 | threshold_crossing]

Every morning starts the same. Sunrise. Valley. Camp. Tents. Oil lamps. No running water. Carter walks through. Checks yesterday's progress. He speaks some Arabic. We speak some English. Mostly, we point. It's 50 degrees Celsius by noon. We've been digging here for six years. Found nothing. But today, when I hit that step, Carter drops to his knees. He's not checking the hole. He's staring. That's when I know. This time is different.

---

[CH05 | 1:25-2:35 | daily_life_exploration]

Now we wait. Carter sends a telegram to England: "At last have made wonderful discovery in Valley; a magnificent tomb with seals intact; re-covered same for your arrival; congratulations." He buries it again. For 19 days, we cover the steps every single evening. If word gets out, tomb robbers come. So every night, sand goes back on. Every morning, we uncover it again. Make sure it's still there. It's still there. The desert doesn't change. We haul water from the Nile. Eat the same flatbread. Same lentils. I sleep in a tent that smells like canvas and dust. I've stayed in worse places. At night, it's cold. During the day, sand too hot to touch bare-handed. We move stones. Carry baskets. Wait. Nineteen days of knowing there's a tomb right under our feet. Can't look inside.

---

[CH06 | 2:35-4:34 | steerage_social_life]

You have to understand. Carter's been looking since 1917. Six years of digging, grid by grid, finding nothing. His sponsor, Lord Carnarvon, had told him: 1922 is the last year. No discovery, no more money. That deadline hangs over all of us. And now, we found it. Carnarvon's sailing from England with his daughter, Lady Evelyn Herbert. She's 20 years old. Keeps a camera. Takes notes. The British call her a "lady." She calls herself lucky. I work next to a man named Ahmed. Three kids. He's saving for a donkey so his son can sell vegetables in Luxor instead of digging. "What do you think is down there?" he asks. I tell him, gold. Maybe. He says, "Even if there's nothing, we were the ones who found the door." That's all he wants. To have found the door. I don't tell him I hope there's more. I watch Carter pace the site every evening. He measures the steps again. Checks the seal. Walks away. Comes back. Carnarvon arrives in 19 days. Tonight, we clear all the steps.

---

[CH07 | 4:34-5:53 | communal_celebration]

November 4th, 1922, morning. I'm clearing rubble from in front of Ramesses VI's tomb. There used to be workers' huts here, 3,000 years ago. We're taking them apart, stone by stone. My shovel goes in. Hits something flat. Not a rock. I call Carter. He comes over. Kneels down. Brushes sand with his hands. A cut stone. A step. We keep going. One step. Two. By noon, we've uncovered twelve. It's a staircase going down. Carter finds a seal on the doorway at the bottom. He can read the hieroglyphs. He looks up. "This is a tomb." Not a storage room. Not a cache. A tomb. Nobody says anything. Ahmed grips my shoulder. We stand there. Staring at a doorway buried since before anyone can remember. Carter's smiling. I've never seen him smile. He stands. Brushes off his knees. Looks at each of us. "We cover it tonight. Tell no one."

---

[CH08 | 5:53-7:10 | confession_and_heist]

Here's the thing. You already know what's inside. I didn't. For 19 days, we didn't know. See, there are signs of ancient break-ins on that sealed door. Robbers got in twice, maybe 3,200 years ago. Right after the burial. The necropolis officials sealed it back up. But we don't know how much they took. Every other royal tomb in this valley has been stripped clean. So for 19 days, we're working on a question: is this another empty room? Carter reburies the stairs. We cover them with sand and stones every night. During the day, we sit in camp. Wait. Ahmed asks, "What if it's empty?" I don't answer. None of us do.

---

[CH09 | 7:10-8:25 | forbidden_luxury_reveal]

November 26th, 1922. Carnarvon's here. We've cleared all sixteen steps. There's a doorway, sealed, with Tutankhamun's name on it. Carter makes a small hole in the top left corner. He lights a candle first—testing for dangerous gases—then reaches in. Carnarvon asks, "Can you see anything?" Carter's silent for a moment. Then: "Yes, wonderful things." Here's what he wrote later: "At first I could see nothing, the hot air escaping from the chamber causing the candle flame to flicker, but presently, as my eyes grew accustomed to the light, details of the room within emerged slowly from the mist, strange animals, statues, and gold. Everywhere the glint of gold." That night, November 26th, four people go in. Carter. His assistant Callender. Carnarvon. Evelyn. They don't tell anyone. They're the first people in 3,300 years to step inside.

---

[CH10 | 8:25-9:19 | luxury_catalog]

The front room. Six chariots, disassembled. Three golden beds shaped like animals. A throne covered in gold and silver, with a painting of the queen anointing the king. Carter calls it the most beautiful object ever found in Egypt. Boxes. Statues. Two life-sized figures of the pharaoh in black and gold, standing guard on either side of the sealed burial chamber door. Beyond that, four nested shrines covered in gold, so large they almost fill the room. Inside those, a stone sarcophagus. Inside that, three coffins. The innermost coffin: 110.4 kilograms of solid gold. The mask on the mummy's face: 10.23 kilograms. In total, 5,398 objects. They'll spend ten years cataloging everything.

---

[CH11 | 9:19-9:55 | dramatic_irony_turn]

But here's what nobody's saying yet. This isn't just treasure. This is a person. Tutankhamun was about 18 years old when he died, around 1323 BC. He ruled for nine years, starting when he was a child. After his death, his name was erased. Official king lists. Later pharaohs pretended he never existed. That's why this tomb survived. Nobody remembered it was here. The burial was rushed. You can see it in the tomb paintings. Brown spots on the wet plaster. Mold grew because they sealed it before the paint dried. Based on documented dates, he was forgotten for 3,245 years.

---

[CH12 | 9:55-10:50 | plan_rehearsal]

Opening the tomb takes ten years. November 1922, we find the steps. February 1923, we open the burial chamber. But the shrines are nested so tightly, they have to be disassembled panel by panel. 1924, Carter walks off the job. The Egyptian government wants control. He refuses. They shut down the dig. 1925, he comes back under a new agreement: everything stays in Egypt. October 28th, 1925, they finally open the innermost golden coffin. That's three years just to reach the innermost coffin. The full excavation takes ten years, until 1932.

---

[CH13 | 10:50-11:25 | futile_warning]

October 1925. Carter opens the innermost coffin. The mummy is completely stuck to the coffin with resin. They have to use heated knives to separate the wrappings. November 11th to 19th, in a temporary laboratory, they unwrap a body wrapped 3,300 years ago. The resin has turned solid. The linen is fused to the gold. Carter writes in his diary: the work is necessary, but every cut feels wrong. "The youthful likeness of Tut-ankh-Amen made us realize the past." This isn't just archaeology. This is touching someone who was buried with care, in a hurry, by people who thought he'd rest undisturbed forever. And here we are. Cutting him free.

---

[CH14 | 11:25-12:21 | countdown_and_impact]

November 11th to 19th, 1925. In a temporary laboratory, they unwrap the mummy. Layer after layer of linen, fused with resin. Then, there it is. The golden mask. 10.23 kilograms of gold. Inlaid with blue glass and semi-precious stones. The face of an 18-year-old king. The eyes are open. They're looking at you. Right now, across 3,245 years, his eyes are looking at the people who opened his tomb. You are standing in 1925, staring at 1323 BC. That's the moment. That's what it means to be first.

---

[CH15 | 12:21-13:17 | collapse_witnessing]

April 5th, 1923. Six months after the discovery. Lord Carnarvon dies in Cairo. A mosquito bite on his cheek. Infected. Turned to blood poisoning. He's 56. The newspapers call it the curse of the pharaohs. 2002, the British Medical Journal does a study. 44 Westerners connected to the excavation. 25 in the exposed group. Average age at death: 70 years. 19 in the unexposed group. Average: 75 years. After adjustment, no statistical difference. But the story sticks. Carter keeps working. He fights with officials. Walks out. Comes back. 1932, the tomb is finally empty. 1939, Carter dies in London. He's 64. Seventeen years after he opened the tomb.

---

[CH16 | 13:17-15:00 | closure_reflection]

November 4th, 1922. My shovel hits a step. I call Carter. We uncover a doorway. For 19 days, we don't know if there's anything inside. November 26th, Carter makes a hole, lights a candle, and says, "Wonderful things." I'm there. Not in the room, but outside. Waiting. Ahmed's next to me. Evelyn's taking photographs. Carnarvon's leaning over Carter's shoulder. We are the first people in 3,245 years to know this tomb exists. The books will say "Tutankhamun's tomb was discovered in 1922." That's true. But it's one thing to read about a discovery. It's another thing to be standing there, in the Valley, in the heat, not knowing what's below, and then seeing gold shine back at you from the dark. The past isn't a story. It's a room you can walk into, if you're the one holding the candle. That's when time stops.

What you're about to see comes from Howard Carter's own book, archive photographs, 1922 site records, and his private papers now held at the Griffith Institute. We've reconstructed it as accurately as possible. What it was actually like to be there. To be the first person in over three millennia to see what's inside.

---

[CH03 | 0:34-0:52 | mission_briefing]

Okay, just between you and me. We're here to do two things. First, prove this isn't another looted tomb. Ancient thieves got into almost every other one. See that sealed door? There are signs it was opened before. Twice. Ancient robbers got in, maybe over 3,000 years ago. The officials sealed it back up. But we don't know how much they took. Every other royal tomb in this valley—stripped clean. Second, witness the moment Carter breaks that seal. The moment he sees what's been sealed since 1323 BC. Let's go in.

---

[CH04 | 0:52-1:25 | threshold_crossing]

Every morning starts the same. Sunrise. Valley. Camp. Tents. Oil lamps. No running water. Carter walks through. Checks yesterday's progress. He knows a little Arabic. I know a little English. Mostly—we just point. That works. It's 50 degrees Celsius by noon. We've been digging here for six years. Found nothing. But today, when I hit that step, Carter drops to his knees. He's not checking the hole. He's staring. That's when I know. This time is different.

---

[CH05 | 1:25-2:35 | daily_life_exploration]

Now we wait. Carter sends a telegram to England: "At last have made wonderful discovery in Valley; a magnificent tomb with seals intact; re-covered same for your arrival; congratulations." He buries it again. For 19 days, we cover the steps every evening. If word gets out, tomb robbers come. Every night, sand goes back on. Every morning, we uncover it again. The desert doesn't change. We haul water. Eat flatbread and lentils. Sleep in tents. At night, it's cold. During the day, too hot to touch bare-handed. We move stones. Carry baskets. Wait. Ahmed asks me at night: "What if it's empty?" I don't answer. Nobody does. Nineteen days of knowing there's a tomb under our feet. We can't look inside.

---

[CH06 | 2:35-4:34 | steerage_social_life]

Ahmed tells me this is Carter's last season. His sponsor—some English lord—won't pay for another year. That's why Carter walks the site every evening. Checking. Measuring. He's running out of time. The lord is sailing from Egypt. Ahmed and I work side by side. Three kids. He's saving for a donkey so his son can sell vegetables in Luxor instead of digging. "What do you think is down there?" he asks. I tell him, gold. Maybe. He says, "Even if there's nothing, we found the door." That's all he wants. To have found the door.

---

[CH07 | 4:34-5:53 | communal_celebration]

November 4th, 1922, morning. I'm clearing rubble from in front of Ramesses VI's tomb. There used to be workers' huts here, 3,000 years ago. We're taking them apart, stone by stone. My shovel goes in. Hits something flat. Not a rock. I call Carter. He comes over. Kneels down. Brushes sand with his hands. A cut stone. A step. We keep going. One step. Two. Three. By noon, we've uncovered most of them. It's a staircase going down. Carter finds a seal on the doorway at the bottom. He can read the hieroglyphs. He looks up. "This is a tomb." Not a storage room. Not a cache. A tomb. A tomb. Not a storage room. Not a cache. A tomb. Someone shouts. Another man drops to his knees, kissing the stone. Ahmed grabs me, shaking my shoulders, laughing. Carter's standing there. He's smiling. Crying. I've never seen him smile. Then he stops. Looks at each of us. His voice drops: "Tonight we cover it. Tell no one. If word gets out, robbers will come before Carnarvon arrives." The joy drains from the air. We stand there. We found it. But we can't tell anyone. That's the price.

---

[CH08 | 5:53-7:10 | confession_and_heist]

---

[CH09 | 7:10-8:25 | forbidden_luxury_reveal]

November 26th, 1922. Carnarvon's here. We've cleared all the steps. There's a doorway, sealed, with Tutankhamun's name on it. Carter makes a small hole in the top left corner. He lights a candle first—testing for gases—then leans in. Hot air rushes out. The candle flickers. Almost dies. I'm standing behind him. Can't see what he sees. Carnarvon asks: "Can you see anything?" Carter doesn't move. Just stares into the dark. His hand is shaking. Then: "Yes. Wonderful things." He leans back. His face is wet. "It's not empty," he says. "There's gold. Everywhere." Later, he writes: everywhere the glint of gold. But in that moment, he can't say more than three words.

---

[CH10 | 8:25-9:19 | luxury_catalog]

November 29th. Official opening. Egyptian officials. Invited guests. We break down the doorway. Step inside. The front room. My eyes don't know where to look. Three beds carved like animals—lion, cow, hippopotamus—covered in gold. Six chariots, disassembled, stacked against the wall. Boxes. Statues. And in the corner, a throne. Gold and silver. A painting on the back: the queen anointing the king. Carter calls it the most beautiful object ever found in Egypt. Then we see them. Two figures, life-sized, standing guard on either side of the burial chamber door. Black skin. Gold kilts. Gold staffs. Their eyes are painted. Staring straight ahead. Guarding what's behind that sealed door. Nobody speaks. We all know what's behind there. Beyond that door, four shrines covered in gold, so large they almost fill the room. Inside those, a stone sarcophagus. Inside that, three coffins. The innermost: 110.4 kilograms of solid gold. The mask: 10.23 kilograms. In total, 5,398 objects. They'll spend ten years recording everything.

---

[CH11 | 9:19-9:55 | dramatic_irony_turn]

But here's what nobody's saying yet. This isn't just treasure. This is a person. Tutankhamun was about 18 years old when he died, around 1323 BC. He ruled for nine years, starting when he was a child. After his death, his name was erased. Official king lists. Later pharaohs pretended he never existed. That's why this tomb survived. Nobody remembered it was here. The burial was rushed. You can see it in the tomb paintings. Brown spots on the wet plaster. Mold grew because they sealed it before the paint dried. From the records we have, he was forgotten for 3,244 years.

---

[CH12 | 9:55-10:50 | plan_rehearsal]

November 1925. Three years have passed. I'm back in the valley. Carter sent word: they're opening the innermost coffin. He wants the man who found the first step to be there. I walk into KV15. They've converted it into a temporary laboratory. There it is. The golden coffin. 110.4 kilograms of solid gold. The mummy inside is completely stuck to the coffin with resin. They've been working for days, heating tools, carefully separating the wrappings. Today is the day. They'll lift the mask.

---

[CH13 | 10:50-11:25 | futile_warning]

November 11th, 1925. KV15 tomb, converted into a laboratory. The golden coffin is open. Inside, the mummy, wrapped in linen, covered in black resin. Hardened. Fused to the gold. Carter lights the heating lamp. The knife glows red. He leans in. The blade touches the resin. A hiss. Smoke. The smell hits me—sharp, ancient, like burned incense and something else I can't name. The resin melts. He cuts. The linen tears. Layer after layer. Black. Brown. Ochre. White. He stops. Wipes his forehead. Looks at us. Nobody speaks. Ahmed is standing in the corner, hands clasped. I step back. Hit the wall. Carter records the difficult process in his notes: the resin forced the team to use heated tools to carefully separate the wrappings. We're cutting through 3,244 years. Every layer of linen is someone's prayer. And we're tearing it open.

---

[CH14 | 11:25-12:21 | countdown_and_impact]

November 19th, 1925. The last layer. Carter's hands are shaking. He grips the edge of the linen. Pulls. Slowly. The fabric resists. Then gives. Gold. Just a sliver at first. Then more. The edge of a headdress. A curve. Carter stops. Takes a breath. Pulls again. The mask emerges. 10.23 kilograms of solid gold. Inlaid with blue glass and lapis lazuli. Everyone steps back. As if pushed. The room goes silent. No camera clicks. No breathing. Just the mask. And then I see them. The eyes. Inlaid. Staring straight ahead. Open. They're looking at you. Not past you. At you. You are standing in a room in 1925, looking at a face from 1323 BC. 3,244 years collapse into this moment. He's been in the dark all this time. Waiting. And now you're here. Someone behind me starts crying. Ahmed drops to his knees. Carter just stares. Nobody speaks. Because there are no words. That's when time stops.

---

[CH15 | 12:21-13:17 | collapse_witnessing]

April 5th, 1923. Six months after the discovery. Lord Carnarvon dies in Cairo. A mosquito bite on his cheek. Infected. Turned to blood poisoning. He's 56. The newspapers call it the curse of the pharaohs. 2002, a study in the British Medical Journal examines the claim. 44 Westerners connected to the excavation. 25 in the exposed group. Average age at death: 70 years. 19 in the unexposed group. Average: 75 years. After adjustment, no statistical difference. But the story sticks. Carter keeps working. He fights with officials. Walks out. Comes back. 1932, the tomb is finally empty. 1939, Carter dies in London. He's 64. Seventeen years after he opened the tomb.

---

[CH16 | 13:17-15:00 | closure_reflection]

November 4th, 1922. My shovel hits a step. I call Carter. We uncover a doorway. For 19 days, we don't know if there's anything inside. November 26th, Carter makes a hole, lights a candle, and says, "Wonderful things." I'm there. Not in the room, but outside. Waiting. Ahmed's next to me. November 19th, 1925. The last layer of linen pulled away. The mask staring back. The room goes silent. Ahmed drops to his knees. That's when time stops. Not because the clock stops. Because you realize you're standing at the edge of 3,000 years. On one side, 1925. On the other, 1323 BC. And between them, just you. Holding a candle. Looking into his eyes. Ahmed bought his donkey in 1926. His son sells vegetables in Luxor market now. Sometimes he points at the museum and tells tourists: my father found that tomb. That's all he wanted. To have been the one who found the door. The books will say "Tutankhamun's tomb was discovered in 1922." That's true. But it's one thing to read about a discovery. It's another thing to be standing there, in the valley, in the heat, not knowing what's below. And then to be there again, three years later, when the last layer of linen is pulled away. When the mask's eyes open. When the room goes silent because no one can breathe. That's what it means to be first.

# I Was the Worker Who Opened Tutankhamun's Tomb - Optimized Script
[CH01 | 0:00-0:20 | immersive_premise_hook]

November 4th, 1922. Valley of the Kings, Egypt. My shovel hits stone. Not just any stone. A step. Something buried underneath. A tomb forgotten for 3,245 years. Inside, 110 kilograms of solid gold. But right now, I'm just a worker getting paid by the day.

---

[CH02 | 0:20-0:34 | authenticity_contract]

What you're about to see comes from Howard Carter's own book, archive photographs, and 1922 site records. We've reconstructed it as accurately as possible. What it was actually like to be there. To be the first person in over three millennia to see what's inside.

---

[CH03 | 0:34-0:52 | mission_briefing]

Okay, just between you and me. We're here to do two things. First, prove this isn't another looted tomb. Ancient thieves got into almost every other one. Second, witness the moment Carter breaks that seal. The moment he sees what's been sealed since 1323 BC. Let's go in.

---

[CH04 | 0:52-1:25 | threshold_crossing]

Every morning starts the same. Sunrise. Valley. Camp. Tents. Oil lamps. No running water. Carter walks through. Checks yesterday's progress. He speaks some Arabic. We speak some English. Mostly, we point. It's 50 degrees Celsius by noon. We've been digging here for six years. Found nothing. But today, when I hit that step, Carter drops to his knees. He's not checking the hole. He's staring. That's when I know. This time is different.

---

[CH05 | 1:25-2:35 | daily_life_exploration]

Now we wait. Carter sends a telegram to England: "At last have made wonderful discovery in Valley; a magnificent tomb with seals intact; re-covered same for your arrival; congratulations." He buries it again. For 19 days, we cover the steps every single evening. If word gets out, tomb robbers come. So every night, sand goes back on. Every morning, we uncover it again. Make sure it's still there. It's still there. The desert doesn't change. We haul water from the Nile. Eat the same flatbread. Same lentils. I sleep in a tent that smells like canvas and dust. I've stayed in worse places. At night, it's cold. During the day, sand too hot to touch bare-handed. We move stones. Carry baskets. Wait. Nineteen days of knowing there's a tomb right under our feet. Can't look inside.

---

[CH06 | 2:35-4:34 | steerage_social_life]

You have to understand. Carter's been looking since 1917. Six years of digging, grid by grid, finding nothing. His sponsor, Lord Carnarvon, had told him: 1922 is the last year. No discovery, no more money. That deadline hangs over all of us. And now, we found it. Carnarvon's sailing from England with his daughter, Lady Evelyn Herbert. She's 20 years old. Keeps a camera. Takes notes. The British call her a "lady." She calls herself lucky. I work next to a man named Ahmed. Three kids. He's saving for a donkey so his son can sell vegetables in Luxor instead of digging. "What do you think is down there?" he asks. I tell him, gold. Maybe. He says, "Even if there's nothing, we were the ones who found the door." That's all he wants. To have found the door. I don't tell him I hope there's more. I watch Carter pace the site every evening. He measures the steps again. Checks the seal. Walks away. Comes back. Carnarvon arrives in 19 days. Tonight, we clear all the steps.

---

[CH07 | 4:34-5:53 | communal_celebration]

November 4th, 1922, morning. I'm clearing rubble from in front of Ramesses VI's tomb. There used to be workers' huts here, 3,000 years ago. We're taking them apart, stone by stone. My shovel goes in. Hits something flat. Not a rock. I call Carter. He comes over. Kneels down. Brushes sand with his hands. A cut stone. A step. We keep going. One step. Two. By noon, we've uncovered twelve. It's a staircase going down. Carter finds a seal on the doorway at the bottom. He can read the hieroglyphs. He looks up. "This is a tomb." Not a storage room. Not a cache. A tomb. Nobody says anything. Ahmed grips my shoulder. We stand there. Staring at a doorway buried since before anyone can remember. Carter's smiling. I've never seen him smile. He stands. Brushes off his knees. Looks at each of us. "We cover it tonight. Tell no one."

---

[CH08 | 5:53-7:10 | confession_and_heist]

Here's the thing. You already know what's inside. I didn't. For 19 days, we didn't know. See, there are signs of ancient break-ins on that sealed door. Robbers got in twice, maybe 3,200 years ago. Right after the burial. The necropolis officials sealed it back up. But we don't know how much they took. Every other royal tomb in this valley has been stripped clean. So for 19 days, we're working on a question: is this another empty room? Carter reburies the stairs. We cover them with sand and stones every night. During the day, we sit in camp. Wait. Ahmed asks, "What if it's empty?" I don't answer. None of us do.

---

[CH09 | 7:10-8:25 | forbidden_luxury_reveal]

November 26th, 1922. Carnarvon's here. We've cleared all sixteen steps. There's a doorway, sealed, with Tutankhamun's name on it. Carter makes a small hole in the top left corner. He lights a candle first—testing for dangerous gases—then reaches in. Carnarvon asks, "Can you see anything?" Carter's silent for a moment. Then: "Yes, wonderful things." Here's what he wrote later: "At first I could see nothing, the hot air escaping from the chamber causing the candle flame to flicker, but presently, as my eyes grew accustomed to the light, details of the room within emerged slowly from the mist, strange animals, statues, and gold. Everywhere the glint of gold." That night, November 26th, four people go in. Carter. His assistant Callender. Carnarvon. Evelyn. They don't tell anyone. They're the first people in 3,300 years to step inside.

---

[CH10 | 8:25-9:19 | luxury_catalog]

The front room. Six chariots, disassembled. Three golden beds shaped like animals. A throne covered in gold and silver, with a painting of the queen anointing the king. Carter calls it the most beautiful object ever found in Egypt. Boxes. Statues. Two life-sized figures of the pharaoh in black and gold, standing guard on either side of the sealed burial chamber door. Beyond that, four nested shrines covered in gold, so large they almost fill the room. Inside those, a stone sarcophagus. Inside that, three coffins. The innermost coffin: 110.4 kilograms of solid gold. The mask on the mummy's face: 10.23 kilograms. In total, 5,398 objects. They'll spend ten years cataloging everything.

---

[CH11 | 9:19-9:55 | dramatic_irony_turn]

But here's what nobody's saying yet. This isn't just treasure. This is a person. Tutankhamun was about 18 years old when he died, around 1323 BC. He ruled for nine years, starting when he was a child. After his death, his name was erased. Official king lists. Later pharaohs pretended he never existed. That's why this tomb survived. Nobody remembered it was here. The burial was rushed. You can see it in the tomb paintings. Brown spots on the wet plaster. Mold grew because they sealed it before the paint dried. Based on documented dates, he was forgotten for 3,245 years.

---

[CH12 | 9:55-10:50 | plan_rehearsal]

Opening the tomb takes ten years. November 1922, we find the steps. February 1923, we open the burial chamber. But the shrines are nested so tightly, they have to be disassembled panel by panel. 1924, Carter walks off the job. The Egyptian government wants control. He refuses. They shut down the dig. 1925, he comes back under a new agreement: everything stays in Egypt. October 28th, 1925, they finally open the innermost golden coffin. That's three years just to reach the innermost coffin. The full excavation takes ten years, until 1932.

---

[CH13 | 10:50-11:25 | futile_warning]

October 1925. Carter opens the innermost coffin. The mummy is completely stuck to the coffin with resin. They have to use heated knives to separate the wrappings. November 11th to 19th, in a temporary laboratory, they unwrap a body wrapped 3,300 years ago. The resin has turned solid. The linen is fused to the gold. Carter writes in his diary: the work is necessary, but every cut feels wrong. "The youthful likeness of Tut-ankh-Amen made us realize the past." This isn't just archaeology. This is touching someone who was buried with care, in a hurry, by people who thought he'd rest undisturbed forever. And here we are. Cutting him free.

---

[CH14 | 11:25-12:21 | countdown_and_impact]

November 11th to 19th, 1925. In a temporary laboratory, they unwrap the mummy. Layer after layer of linen, fused with resin. Then, there it is. The golden mask. 10.23 kilograms of gold. Inlaid with blue glass and semi-precious stones. The face of an 18-year-old king. The eyes are open. They're looking at you. Right now, across 3,245 years, his eyes are looking at the people who opened his tomb. You are standing in 1925, staring at 1323 BC. That's the moment. That's what it means to be first.

---

[CH15 | 12:21-13:17 | collapse_witnessing]

April 5th, 1923. Six months after the discovery. Lord Carnarvon dies in Cairo. A mosquito bite on his cheek. Infected. Turned to blood poisoning. He's 56. The newspapers call it the curse of the pharaohs. 2002, the British Medical Journal does a study. 44 Westerners connected to the excavation. 25 in the exposed group. Average age at death: 70 years. 19 in the unexposed group. Average: 75 years. After adjustment, no statistical difference. But the story sticks. Carter keeps working. He fights with officials. Walks out. Comes back. 1932, the tomb is finally empty. 1939, Carter dies in London. He's 64. Seventeen years after he opened the tomb.

---

[CH16 | 13:17-15:00 | closure_reflection]

November 4th, 1922. My shovel hits a step. I call Carter. We uncover a doorway. For 19 days, we don't know if there's anything inside. November 26th, Carter makes a hole, lights a candle, and says, "Wonderful things." I'm there. Not in the room, but outside. Waiting. Ahmed's next to me. Evelyn's taking photographs. Carnarvon's leaning over Carter's shoulder. We are the first people in 3,245 years to know this tomb exists. The books will say "Tutankhamun's tomb was discovered in 1922." That's true. But it's one thing to read about a discovery. It's another thing to be standing there, in the Valley, in the heat, not knowing what's below, and then seeing gold shine back at you from the dark. The past isn't a story. It's a room you can walk into, if you're the one holding the candle. That's when time stops.
